_comment: Fallback Ambient-AI-style note for Claire, loaded when ?mock=1 is present or when Quo returns no call. Ambient format references: Abridge, Nabla, DeepScribe public sample output.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, this is SurveyHealth calling from Providence Family Clinic. May I speak with Claire?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, this is Claire.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi Claire, this is your monthly check-in. Do you have about five minutes to go through a few questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. In the past week, have you had any new or worsening symptoms — anything like shortness of breath, chest pain, or dizziness?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Well, I have been more short of breath than usual. When I walk up the stairs at my daughter's house I have to stop halfway now. That's new.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. How long has that been going on?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: About a week, maybe nine days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been taking all your medications on schedule?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, my daughter sets them out for me. I take the water pill in the morning and the heart pill at dinner.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great to hear. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: A little bit in my ankles in the evenings, yes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been able to check your weight this week?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I weighed yesterday. 164, so up about three pounds from last week.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. How have you been sleeping?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Not great. I've been waking up needing to prop up on pillows to breathe easier.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay, I'm going to flag that for your care team. Have you had any chest pain or heart palpitations?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No chest pain. Heart feels normal.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good. Any changes to your diet or appetite?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Appetite is fine. I've been trying to watch my salt like they said.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's really good. Would you like to speak with a nurse today about the shortness of breath and weight gain?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I think that would be a good idea.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'll have a nurse call you back within the next two hours. Is this the best number to reach you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, this is my home phone.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Thank you for your time Claire, and we'll be in touch soon.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, bye.

note.chiefComplaint: Increased dyspnea on exertion and bilateral ankle edema over the past 7–9 days, with a 3-lb weight gain from the prior week and new orthopnea.
note.hpi: Ms. Henderson is a 77-year-old female with a history of heart failure and hypertension enrolled in CCM. She reports progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs, now limiting her activity after half a flight. Symptoms began approximately 7–9 days ago. She notes mild bilateral ankle swelling in the evenings and a 3-pound weight gain over the last week. She is waking overnight with orthopnea and needing to prop up on pillows. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or new cough. Medication adherence reported as good (furosemide AM, lisinopril with dinner) with daughter assisting. Adherence to low-sodium diet reported.
note.reviewOfSystems: CARDIOVASCULAR — positive for DOE and bilateral lower-extremity edema; negative for chest pain and palpitations. PULMONARY — positive for orthopnea; negative for cough and wheeze. GI — appetite intact, denies nausea. NEURO — denies dizziness or syncope. PSYCH — denies depressed mood; PHQ-2 not administered this visit.
note.assessment: Likely early decompensation of chronic heart failure — weight gain, new orthopnea, worsening DOE, and ankle edema are consistent with volume overload. Medication adherence does not appear to be the driver. No red flags (no chest pain, no syncope) but pattern warrants same-day clinical review.
note.plan:
1. Nurse callback within 2 hours to assess need for diuretic dose adjustment vs. same-day clinic visit.
2. Recommend daily AM weight log for next 7 days; alert threshold +2 lb/day or +5 lb/week.
3. Reinforce strict 2g sodium diet and fluid intake guidance.
4. Continue furosemide and lisinopril as prescribed pending nurse review.
5. If symptoms worsen before callback (chest pain, severe SOB at rest, lightheadedness) — instruct patient to call 911.
note.patientEducation: Discussed warning signs of heart failure decompensation. Reviewed daily weight monitoring rationale and when to call. Patient verbalized understanding and agreed to callback.
note.followUp: Nurse callback today (< 2 hours). Next scheduled CCM check-in in 7 days. PCP informed via tasking.

summary.oneLine: Likely early CHF decompensation — 3-lb weight gain, new orthopnea, worsening DOE, mild ankle edema; nurse callback within 2 hours requested.
